s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, severe, mechanical low back pain and mental depression with cutaneous and subcutaneous lesions and muscle contractures
salient_findings: Large and deep, irregularly shaped, cutaneous ulcer on the forearm
Woody induration of skin on forearms and abdominal region
Bilateral contracture of deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles
key_facts: 7-year history of severe, mechanical, low back pain
Long-standing mental depression
Current medications include duloxetine hydrochloride, clonazepam, oxcarbazepine, fentanyl, sulpiride, zopiclone, omeprazole magnesium, and baclofen
Self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, 100 mg 4 times per day, for the past 3 years
Cutaneous ulcer on the dorsum of right forearm with necrotic tissue and muscle exposure
Elevated serum creatinine kinase (192 U/L)
Normal complete blood cell count
Normal erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Normal antinuclear antibody
Normal rheumatoid factor
Histopathology shows lobular panniculitis, subcutaneous fat lobules with necrotic adipocytes and dense inflammatory infiltrates
Severe fibrosis in deep dermis and subcutaneous septa
Foreign-body giant cells and macrophages with large, foamy cytoplasm present

shortlist.label: Meperidine-induced fibrosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of subcutaneous meperidine injections and presence of cutaneous ulcers and fibrosis

shortlist.label: Skin popping syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of subcutaneous injections and presence of cutaneous ulcers and fibrosis

shortlist.label: Panniculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology shows lobular panniculitis and necrotic adipocytes

shortlist.label: Lipodermatosclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of cutaneous ulcers and fibrosis, consistent with chronic venous insufficiency

shortlist.label: Complex regional pain syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of severe, mechanical low back pain and presence of muscle contractures

raw.rationale: The patient's history of self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, presence of cutaneous ulcers, and histopathology showing lobular panniculitis and foreign-body giant cells are consistent with skin popping syndrome, a condition characterized by skin and soft tissue damage due to chronic injection of drugs

rejected.label: Meperidine-induced fibrosis
rejected.why: While meperidine use is a factor, the condition is more accurately described by the broader category of skin popping syndrome

rejected.label: Panniculitis
rejected.why: Panniculitis is a feature of the condition, but it is not the most comprehensive diagnosis

rejected.label: Lipodermatosclerosis
rejected.why: Lipodermatosclerosis is a condition that affects the lower legs and is not consistent with the patient's presentation of ulcers and fibrosis in various areas

rejected.label: Complex regional pain syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of severe low back pain, the primary features of the condition are skin and soft tissue damage, not consistent with complex regional pain syndrome
